Title: [from] Matthew Henson: Explorer of the Arctic
Subtitle: The story of the African American adventurer who, steps ahead of Robert E. Peary, became the first man to reach the North Pole...
Author: by Scarlett N. Rebman
Content:
:box:`bbtext(Characters)`

`bbtext(MATTHEW A. HENSON)`, an African American explorer
`bbtext(ADAM)`, Matthew's friend
`bbtext(MR. STEINMETZ)`, Matthew's boss
R`bbtext(OBERT E. PEARY)`, arctic explorer
SCENE 1
`bbtext(TIME)`: `text(Spring, 1887)`.
SETTING: Steinmetz's hat store in
Washington, D.C. Cardboard boxes are piled
up left, as if in a storage room. A store
counter down right has sign in front that
reads, Steinmetz's Hats. Several hats
are on display. Cash register, if available, is
also on counter.
`bbtext(AT RISE)`: MR. STEINMETZ is standing at
the counter, examining an account book.
MATTHEW and ADAM enter left, carrying
boxes. They pause center.
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: We've received the new
shipment of hats, sir. Just arrived on the
train from New York.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Splendid! I didn't expect it
for a few more `text(days)`. Take the boxes to the
store room, please. (MATTHEW and ADAM
cross up left. They carefully place their boxes
on the others.)
`bbtext(MATTHEW)` (Sighing): I tell you, Adam,
I'm growing weary of stocking hats.
`bbtext(ADAM)`: You keep saying that, but
Mr. Steinmetz pays a fair wage. You'd be
a fool to give it up.
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: I know, but I'm restless.
When I close my eyes at night, I feel the
salty sea breeze upon my face. I see ports
in China and North Africa. I remember
the exhilaration of setting sail, of bidding
farewell to the States, of seeing how other
people live.
`bbtext(ADAM)`: You were a sailor? But you're only
`text(twenty-one)`!
`bbtext(MATTHEW)` (Sitting on a stool): Didn't I
tell you? I ran away from my aunt's house
when I was `text(twelve)`. I hung around the docks
until I met a captain who agreed to take me
on board as a cabin boy. Captain Childs
had a beautiful merchant ship, the Katie
Hines. He didn't know what to make of a
scruffy orphan boy in dirty rags that passed
for clothes, but for some reason, he took a
liking to me and taught me to read and
write, as well as sail.
`bbtext(ADAM)`: Then why did you give it up?
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: Because most captains don't
bother to look past the color of a man's skin
to recognize his abilities. When Captain
Childs died, I gave up the sea. Instead, I
found jobs like this `text(one)`. I thought it would
be enough, thought about settling down and
starting a family. But my imagination is
overactive. `text(Every night)` I dream about the
journeys I might take, the stories I might
write down.
`bbtext(ADAM)`: Matthew, don't take this the wrong
way, but I think you're plumb crazy. Making
a decent wage is all I want out of life. A
decent wage and a decent wife. But you're
right, not much out of the ordinary happens
at Steinmetz's. (Bell jingles, as if a door
opened, and PEARY enters. He looks around
the shop.)
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Good afternoon, sir. Can I
help you find something?
`bbtext(PEARY)` (Distracted): Yes, a hat, please.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Then you've come to the
right place. Were you looking for a certain
type? Perhaps a bowler for a `text(Sunday)` walk?
Or a top hat for an evening at the opera?
`bbtext(PEARY)`: No, no ... I need a sun hat.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Hmmm. That's an unusual
request. Let me call `text(one)` of my boys. He
knows where everything is around here.
Matthew! (MATTHEW crosses up center.)
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: Yes, sir?
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: This gentleman is looking for
a sun hat. Could you be more specific about
your needs, Mr... ?
`bbtext(PEARY)`: Peary-Lieutenant Peary, civil
engineer for the United States Navy. I
am about to leave for an expedition to
Nicaragua,* and I hear the sun and heat are
brutal there. Do you have any appropriate
head gear?
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Well, Matthew, do we have
something to suit the gentleman's needs?
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: Yes, I believe we do. Excuse
me, I'll be right back. (MATTHEW goes to
storeroom, looks through boxes.)
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Tell me, Lieutenant, what
will you be doing in Nicaragua?
`bbtext(PEARY)`: Our expedition is to determine
whether a canal could be constructed to
connect the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Your work sounds very
interesting, Lieutenant. And arduous.
`bbtext(PEARY)`: Yes, it is. I traveled to the Arctic
`text(last year)`, so a tropical climate may be a
shock to my system. (Pacing) There are so
many details to keep track of. I really could
use an assistant to accompany me.
(MATTHEW returns with a hat in his hands.)
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: Ah, here we are! Please, try
it on. There is a mirror on the wall if you
need `text(one)`. (MATTHEW hands PEARY the
hat.)
`bbtext(PEARY)`: No need for a mirror. This is
exactly what I wanted. I'll take it.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)` (Glancing from PEARY to
MATTHEW): You know, Lieutenant, if you
are looking for an assistant, Matthew here
has had some experience with trips abroad.
`bbtext(PEARY)`: Oh?
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: Yes, sir. I was a sailor for
several `text(years)`.
`bbtext(STEINMETZ)`: He is my most reliable and
competent worker. I certainly recommend
him for your position. I would hate to lose
him, but I suspect that Matthew would have
left me sooner rather than later anyway.
`bbtext(PEARY)`: Well, what do you say? Would you
be willing to travel to Nicaragua with me as
my assistant?
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: Yes, Lieutenant. I would like
that very much. There's only `text(one)` problem.
`bbtext(PEARY)`: What's that?
`bbtext(MATTHEW)`: We had only `text(one)` sun hat left
in stock, and I suspect now I'll be needing
`text(one)` as well. (Blackout)
